title: The Warning Nobody Read: Capturing What Qt Prints So That a Test Can Fail On It

questions.question: A QML handler throws a ReferenceError. What happens to the load?
options: It succeeds, and a warning is printed
questions.explanation: The component created its object and the scope kept one warning.

questions.question: Where does a Qt warning go by default?
options: To standard error, where a test run does not look
questions.explanation: A suite can pass with forty warnings in its log.

questions.question: Why does the scope restore the previous handler?
options: A handler that stays installed after the scope is a function writing into a destroyed object
questions.explanation: After the scopes the old handler was back and saw 2.

questions.question: Two scopes are nested. Where does a message printed between them go?
questions.explanation: The outer kept the messages printed outside the inner scope.

questions.question: Why is the list of messages guarded by a mutex?
options: Qt calls the handler from whichever thread printed

questions.question: What does forward do?
options: Passes each message to the previous handler as well as keeping it
questions.explanation: Both messages were kept and the old handler saw both.
